newsitem.title: USA: ValuJet plans to resume Dallas flights.
newsitem.headline: ValuJet plans to resume Dallas flights.

text.p: ValuJet Airlines on Thursday announced plans to resume flight operations to Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport on April 10.

The airline plans four daily round trip flights on peak travel days between Atlanta and Dallas/Fort Worth. The scheduled expansion increases ValuJets operations to 154 daily departures on peak travel days to 22 cities.
ValuJet will waive its advance purchase requirement for travel completed by April 30, 1997, and sell every seat on every flight between Atlanta and Dallas/Fort Worth for $69 one-way.
Also during April, ValuJet will waive its advance purchase requirement for travel between Dallas/Fort Worth and 18 other ValuJet markets, including seven Florida destinations.

These one-way fares will range from $99 to $149 and travel must be completed by April 30, 1997 and require 14-day advance purchase. After April 30, 1997, the lowest one-way fares between Atlanta and Dallas/Fort Worth will begin at $69.
The airline on February 20 resumed flights to Boston.
Valujet was grounded for safety concerns in June after flight 592 crashed into the Everglades, killing all 110 people aboard. It announced plans to resume services September 26.
